evaluations.note: 16 on the reference machine since the HPO data hold the free energy and the Cauchy stress (2026-10-01; 30 before, 16 before the neighbour lists were exact). BFGS reaches the upper bound RCUT2B = 6.0 at eval 9 (1.015561e-01; the re-evaluation at eval 10 comes out at the rounding level below it and is the best), takes the one-sided gradient there (evals 11-12), re-evaluates the bound (13-14), takes the gradient again (15-16) and ends (status COMPLETED). Example 05, the same search with the parametric cohesive-energy script, runs to MAXEVAL = 30 instead. Whether BFGS's line search accepts a re-evaluation of the clamped bound depends on the sign of the ~1e-13 relative re-evaluation noise of the warm-started lattice relaxation, so the count is not pinned (evals_tol 14: 2..30, see tolerance_rationale); best loss, components and RCUT2B do not depend on it.

tolerance_rationale: Best loss, components and RCUT2B are pinned at the default tolerances. The evaluation count is not deterministic across machines: the optimum is on the clamped bound RCUT2B = 6.0 (eval 9), and whether DLIB:BFGS's line search accepts a re-evaluation there depends on the sign of a ~1e-13 relative, rounding-level drift of the warm-started lattice relaxation. With the HPO data holding the free energy and the Cauchy stress (2026-10-01) the run ends after 16 evaluations on the reference machine (3 repeated runs identical); it ran to MAXEVAL = 30 with the energies without entropy, as example 05 now does; evals_tol 14 accepts 2..30. The status is COMPLETED either way.
